subject.title: I updated Scrapling and the skill became hidden again

question: Should the current Scrapling hide be restored as a false positive, kept hidden under scraping/content policy, or treated as a publish/update visibility regression that needs a code fix?
rationale: The decisive evidence is private production moderation and audit state plus maintainer policy intent for scraping skills; source inspection alone cannot safely unlock a security-hidden public listing.

options.title: Review production state and restore if false positive
options.body: Inspect the current skill, version, scan, and audit records, then restore or apply a manual override if the hide was unintended.

options.title: Keep hidden under policy
options.body: If scraping policy now requires this listing to remain hidden, explain that to the reporter and link the decision back to the open content-policy RFC.

options.title: Open a focused code fix
options.body: If production state shows the update workflow wrongly hides previously clean versions, keep this issue open as the user-facing report and patch that path with regression coverage.

recommendation.title: Review production state and restore if false positive
recommendation.body: Inspect the current skill, version, scan, and audit records, then restore or apply a manual override if the hide was unintended.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen owns the most relevant recent moderation, ClawScan, pending-publish, and prior Scrapling incident history in the evidence trail.
